title: Streaming multipart requests scramble tool invocation headers in Dedicated VPC (customer escalation)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers on Dedicated VPC reported that when they use streaming multipart tool invocation (mixing text + JSON tool payloads) the server-sent headers that correlate streamed chunks to a specific tool invocation are sometimes reordered or duplicated, causing the structured output assembler to attach fragments to the wrong tool call. Impacted environments: Dedicated pools with customer-side TCP proxies and Private customers behind our proxy adapter. Observed symptoms: 1) Tool A receives fragments that belong to Tool B (mis-attribution). 2) Final structured JSON parse fails intermittently with field mismatches. 3) Errors spike during bursts and when requests cross an internal batching boundary. Repro steps (internal): 1) Use benchmark client that simulates 50 concurrent streaming multipart invokes across two tool types with small alternating chunk sizes. 2) Configure a dedicated pool with proxy-adapter enabled and a short network MTU to force chunk fragmentation. 3) Observe chunk headers: some sequence IDs are reused or the correlation header (X-RW-Invoke-ID) is delayed in reordering. Root-cause hypothesis: Timing window in our streaming sequencer allows header/frame metadata to be emitted out-of-order when fragments from different tool calls are multiplexed onto the same connection and the proxy adapter applies head compression. A race in the sequencer's header-emission path + proxy-level compression leads to header -> payload misalignment under certain MTU and batching conditions. Immediate mitigation applied: 2026-03-11 disabled head-compression in proxy-adapter for affected Dedicated pools and added server-side heuristic to reject obviously misordered frames rather than attempting in-place reassembly (avoids misattribution but increases token latency). Customer workarounds provided: 1) Reduce concurrency or disable streaming to fall back to non-streaming calls. 2) Apply temporary edge config to avoid adapter head-compression. Next steps (plan): 1) Harden sequencer to include per-chunk monotonically-increasing sequence numbers and verify that header and payload are atomically emitted (code change in runtime sequencer). 2) Add end-to-end tests exercising proxy compression + small-MTU fragmentation. 3) Ship canary runtime change to a subset of Dedicated pools and one Private pilot customer. 4) Add metrics for header/payload misalignment and alerting. 5) Post-mortem and customer-facing writeup. Related customer cases: CS-8941, CS-8980. Affects: 3 enterprise customers using Dedicated VPC, intermittent reports from 2 Private deployments. Priority: P0 because it causes incorrect tool outputs and data correctness issues for production traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Sequencer emits atomic header+payload with monotonic per-chunk seq id
Reproducer that triggers misattribution no longer fails after change on canary
Regression tests cover proxy adapter compression + small MTU fragmentation
Canary in Dedicated pool shows <1 reported misattribution for 48h before rollout
